_comment: The GCP environment's single source of truth, the same role clusters/onprem/nodes.json plays
for the on-prem substrate (ADR-0008): every value that could disagree with reality comes from
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS FILE: the billing account ID. It is not a credential -
knowing one grants nothing - but this repository is public, and a billing account ID is the
one value here that identifies a payment instrument. It is passed as TF_VAR_billing_account
instead, and `make gcp-guardrails` says so. The cost is that a fresh clone needs one
environment variable before the guardrail can be applied, which is the same honest shape as
.cache/vault-init.json: reproducible given one thing a human holds.
_project_comment: The project for THIS lab, created 2026-10-31. `make gcp-guardrails` refuses to run while
this is empty rather than defaulting to whatever gcloud happens to be pointed at.
It was briefly set to `shopverse-lab`, which was wrong: that project belongs to an
earlier, abandoned attempt and I took it from `gcloud projects list` without asking
which of the two projects was ours. Recorded because the consequence was not
hypothetical - the first guardrail apply enabled two APIs on somebody else's project.
ONE PROJECT PER LAB, and the reason is teardown rather than tidiness. Deleting a GCP
PROJECT removes everything inside it - buckets, KMS keyrings, clusters, addresses,
disks - in a single action, with 30 days to undo. That is a stronger guarantee than
any resource-by-resource sweep, because a sweep is only as wide as the list of
resource types someone remembered to put in it, and `make cost-check` has now been
too narrow twice in one day.
So: `make gcp-down` is the normal teardown, and `gcloud projects delete <id>` is the
one that cannot miss anything. The budget guardrail survives both - it is attached to
the BILLING ACCOUNT, not the project (ADR-0019 Decision 1), which is exactly the
The project itself is created by hand, once, and that is deliberate: it is the
container the Terraform state lives inside, so it cannot be created by that state.
_zone_comment: ZONAL, never regional. ADR-0003: GKE's free tier covers the cluster management fee for ONE
zonal cluster per billing account per month and does not cover a regional one, where the fee
is charged per cluster. A regional cluster also triples the control plane and the node count.
asia-south1-a (Mumbai) because it is nearest, so kubectl and the storefront are responsive.
The trade against us-central1 is spot capacity: if a spot pool cannot be filled here, the
answer is to change this value and re-apply, not to drop spot.
_budget_comment: ADR-0003 Decision 3: this must exist BEFORE the first cloud resource, which is why it is a
separate Terraform state in terraform/gcp/guardrails and a separate `make gcp-guardrails`.
A guardrail applied in the same run as the thing it guards is not a guardrail.
Scoped to the whole BILLING ACCOUNT rather than to one project, deliberately: a budget that
only watches the project you remembered to filter on is silent about the one you forgot.
_nodes_comment: EXTERNAL IPs ON THE NODES, and this is the decision with a real cost attached - recorded
here rather than discovered on a bill.
ShopVerse's seven images are on ghcr.io. ADR-0003 forbids NAT gateways, and a GKE node with
no external IP and no Cloud NAT cannot reach ghcr.io at all: Private Google Access covers
Google's own services and nothing else. So the options were external IPs, Cloud NAT
(forbidden, and the expensive one), or mirroring the images into Artifact Registry.
External IPs chosen for the first build because it needs no change to the tenant's chart.
GCP bills external IPv4 at roughly $0.005 per address per hour, so two nodes for a
three-hour session is about 3 rupees - not zero, and the reason ADR-0003's target is '₹0
steady-state' rather than '₹0 ever'. `make down` ends the charge.
Mirroring into Artifact Registry is genuinely ₹0 within the 0.5 GB free tier and is the
better end state; it costs a mirroring step and a global.imageRegistry override in the gcp
overlay, which is exactly what the overlay mechanism exists for. Parked, not rejected.
pd-standard rather than pd-balanced: the free tier includes 30 GB-months of pd-standard.
32 GB x 2 nodes exceeds that, so the disks are the other small non-zero line - visible here
